items.t: Hockaday is a small board sub-area in north-central Coquitlam around Pinetree Way and Pinewood Avenue, on the Town Centre side of the city, in the wider Mundy Park / Como Lake orbit of central-north Coquitlam. "Hockaday" is the GVR sub-area name as it appears in the SnapStats GVR September 2026 report for Coquitlam; an official City of Coquitlam neighbourhood plan name and planning area for Hockaday were not confirmed — not verified. No City neighbourhood plan boundary is stated on a City page in the sources read, so street-by-street boundaries are not verified; the working anchors are Pinetree Way and Pinewood Avenue, with Pinetree Secondary verified at 3000 Pinewood Avenue.

Where the condo stock concentrates: nowhere —. The streets around the anchors (McTavish Court, Pipeline Place, Pipeline Road, El Camino Drive, Hockaday Street) list as detached houses in the sources checked.
Nearby areas: Central Coquitlam to the south, Canyon Springs and the City Centre / Town Centre Park area to the north and east, Eagle Ridge to the west, and Burke Mountain beyond to the north-east.
Hockaday is the smallest market in this batch.
The in-area anchor is a school, not a building.
Two neighbouring clusters do the condo work for this whole corridor.

The detached stock is executive-house scale. The Hockaday listing index shows large single-family homes on McTavish Court and Pipeline Place (3,400–5,100 sq ft in the listings checked) — the sub-area's price conversation is a detached conversation, priced against the Coquitlam detached median of $1,455,000, not against any strata figure.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Hockaday

items.t: City zoning frame: Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996 — small-scale residential zones R-1, R-2 and R-3; minimum lot size for subdivision is 650 m² with 18.5 m width for R-1 and R-3, and 465 m² with 12.5 m width for R-2. The provincial small-scale multi-unit housing (SSMUH) rules as adopted in Coquitlam allow up to 3 units on lots 280 m² or smaller and up to 4 units on lots larger than 280 m² and under 4,050 m², including secondary suites and carriage or laneway homes; lots not connected to municipal water or sewer are outside the SSMUH rules, so property-level septic or well status: Not verified.

Strata rules — stated for completeness, because there is no verified strata stock to apply them to: if a strata townhouse is ever marketed in Hockaday, the diligence frame is Form B under Strata Property Act s. 59 (monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies, CRF balance, insurance summary, rules, budget, Rental Disclosure Statement and depreciation report attached; within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page); depreciation reports every five years for strata corporations with five or more lots since July 1, 2024; a CRF minimum contribution of 10% of the annual operating budget since Nov 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since Nov 24, 2022; and only 55+ age bylaws valid since Nov 24, 2022 (SPA ss. 123.1/123.2 + Regulation 7.01, exemptions expanded May 1, 2023).

Fee-simple reality in Hockaday: the verified stock is fee-simple detached housing — NO strata, NO Form B, NO strata fees. A Hockaday house with a suite is still a fee-simple house, not a townhouse complex.

Hazards: the Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area covers all areas within 30 metres of the top of bank or top of ravine bank of any watercourse in this part of Coquitlam; Zoning Bylaw s.519 sets flood protection setbacks from watercourses and s.523 covers riparian areas; a floodplain designation for Hockaday's residential streets: Not verified.

The name itself is the trap. No City of Coquitlam neighbourhood plan name, official planning area or boundary for "Hockaday" was confirmed on a City page — the name lives in the board sub-area system and the SnapStats Coquitlam rows. Always write "Hockaday, Coquitlam": a comp pull from another municipality's similarly named street will corrupt the price evidence.

Even the origin of the name is unverified: no City, museum or archives history source specific to Hockaday was verified pass — including where "Hockaday" comes from: Not verified. Do not invent a namesake story for marketing copy.
The library anchor is on Pinetree Way: Coquitlam Public Library's City Centre branch is at 1169 Pinetree Way, the nearest full branch; the Poirier branch is at 575 Poirier Street.

The nearest hospital is across the municipal border: Eagle Ridge Hospital, 475 Guildford Way, Port Moody (Fraser Health), on the Port Moody / Coquitlam border, is the nearest hospital for this area; Coquitlam urgent and primary care centre locations: Not verified.

City Centre amenities are north-east, not in-area: the City Centre Aquatic Complex and Evergreen Cultural Centre sit in the City Centre area beyond the sub-area — their addresses were not confirmed in the sources read, so distance claims for a specific Hockaday address are not verified until measured.

Coquitlam's 2021 Census population was 148,625, up 6.7% from 139,284 in 2016 (Statistics Canada, 2021 Census, Focus on Geography Series) — city context only; a Hockaday-only population figure: Not verified.

Established-street house lots: The housing sits under the City's small-scale residential zones (R-1, R-2, R-3) around Pinewood Avenue, with Pinetree Secondary as the in-area anchor. A fee-simple lot carries NO strata, NO Form B and NO strata fees.

Lot character, only: subdivision minimums under Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996 are 650 m² with 18.5 m width in R-1 and R-3, and 465 m² with 12.5 m width in R-2; SSMUH unit counts turn on the 280 m² and 4,050 m² thresholds. These are zone minimums and thresholds, not a claim about any existing lot's size — the zone and dimensions of a specific lot are confirmed parcel by parcel, not verified for any individual lot here.
Serviced position, as the City states it: Property-level septic or well status is not verified; confirm the specific lot's connections with the City before pricing any unit potential.

ALR vs non-ALR: ALR status for the sub-area is not verified; ALR status for a specific property is checked in the Agricultural Land Commission's ALR Property and Map Finder. No ALR parcel and no ALR percentage split is stated.

Hazard position: the Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area covers all areas within 30 metres of the top of bank or top of ravine bank of any watercourse in this part of Coquitlam; Zoning Bylaw s.519 sets flood protection setbacks from watercourses and s.523 covers riparian areas; a floodplain designation for Hockaday's residential streets is not verified. Lot-level watercourse / flood status is a property-specific check.

Assemblies / development sites / rezoning proposals: none documented as inventory: The city-wide OCP and the Transit-Oriented Areas work near Pinetree Way apply around the sub-area — planning frameworks, not assemblies and not for-sale land.

Historic subdivisions = built lot fabric, not offerings: the Pinewood Avenue street fabric is established built housing stock; nothing in it is presented as a current lot offering, and the origin of the Hockaday name itself is not verified (no City, museum or archives history source specific to Hockaday was verified).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Hockaday

items.t: ALR rules (for completeness — no Hockaday ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR.
Any history or plan claim for Hockaday beyond the board sub-area name is not verified.

The in-area anchor is a secondary school, and its own address settles its own catchment only: Pinetree Secondary is verified at 3000 Pinewood Avenue, inside the working anchors, and the locator run for that address returned Walton Elementary / Scott Creek Middle / Pinetree Secondary — a neat chain that still does not transfer one street over, because SD43 catchments are address-based.
